prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"The visible columns are clear and the SKUs stay intact, but Price begins beyond the viewport, so comparison requires early horizontal scrolling."},"B":{"grade":"bad","why":"Headers, SKUs, values and tracking identifiers break into narrow vertical fragments, making rows and columns very difficult to scan."},"C":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Most visible fields are legible, but each SKU occupies four lines, weakening row rhythm and making identifiers harder to compare."},"D":{"grade":"bad","why":"Many headers, numbers and identifiers split across lines; the resulting tall rows are difficult to read and compare."},"E":{"grade":"good","why":"The visible rows are compact, with SKUs breaking at hyphens, but the Price values sit against the viewport edge and require scrolling to see comfortably."},"F":{"grade":"good","why":"The visible rows have a compact rhythm, SKUs break at hyphens, and complete Price values fit within the viewport."}},"best":["F"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"The supplied views show only the left portion of each table, so the widths and readability of later columns, especially Warehouse and Tracking, cannot be fully assessed."}
